industry: Tutoring centers, test prep, in-home tutors, daycare, preschool, after-school, and enrichment programs
words_and_claims_to_avoid: 'Raise SAT/ACT [X]–[Y] points' (GOLD-tutoring-childcare-043) unless the center can substantiate typical results for similar students (FTC Act s.5 / 16 CFR 255)
'Guaranteed grade improvement' / 'honor roll guaranteed' without conditions and proof
'Licensed' / 'accredited' / 'universal Pre-K' / 'accepts [subsidy]' unless currently true for that site
'Free week' that quietly requires nonrefundable fees or long lock-ins without clear disclosure (16 CFR 251; state contract rules)
Student photos or quotes without parent/guardian written consent; never collect data from children under 13 online without verifiable parental consent (COPPA)
Implying use of school student records in marketing (FERPA restricts educational agencies/institutions; don't claim improper data use)
Discriminatory enrollment language; follow applicable civil-rights and state licensing advertising rules (equal opportunity)
compliance_notes: FTC Act s.5: score gains, rank improvements, and 'guaranteed results' need substantiation before mailing.
16 CFR 255: parent/student testimonials imply typical results; disclose material connections; 'results not typical' is not a cure-all.
16 CFR 251/233: free registration / $X off / 'value' claims need real base prices and conditions beside the offer.
COPPA: QR landing pages that collect info from under-13s need verifiable parental consent; prefer parent-only forms.
State child-care licensing: advertising must not misrepresent ratios, ages, hours, or license status; many states require license number on ads—verify locally.
Lottery/scratch-off 'win free months' (GOLD-tutoring-childcare-047): 39 USC 3001(k) / contest rules; no-purchase-necessary if chance + consideration.
39 USC 3001: no official school-district/census look-alike mailers.
Fair Housing Act generally does not govern ordinary childcare enrollment ads; still avoid discriminatory preference language under civil-rights and licensing norms.
standing_rules: Emotion-agnostic within the law; fear-of-falling-behind is allowed when factual and paired with a real offer.
Every angle and combo includes sell_the_outcome_line.
Never invent score gains, waitlist lengths, or licensing claims.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: GOLD-tutoring-childcare-043 style 'Raise your SAT score by 250–450 points' vs FTC substantiation rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: do not use point-gain ranges unless the client has competent and reliable evidence of typical results for similar students.

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Scratch-off / prize tutoring passes (GOLD-tutoring-childcare-047) vs mail sweepstakes rules
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Compliance wins: chance promotions need proper rules and no-purchase-necessary language where required (39 USC 3001(k)).

emotion_by_offer_conflicts.conflict: Fear-of-falling-behind headlines vs desire for warm brand tone
emotion_by_offer_conflicts.resolution: Not a legal conflict: emotion-agnostic—client chooses; if fear is used, pair with a real easy action (free assessment/tour) per EPPM logic.
